name: CG Power & Industrial Solutions Ltd
about: CG Power & Industrial Solutions is a global enterprise providing end-to-end solutions to utilities, industries and consumers for the management and application of efficient and sustainable electrical energy. It offers products, services and solutions in two main business segments, viz. Power Systems and Industrial Systems.

flags.text: Revenue compounded 33.2% a year over 5 years but profit shrank 1.3% a year: growth is getting less profitable
Cash conversion cycle stretched from 15 to 48 days in three years
Capital work-in-progress is 34% of fixed assets: a big build-out is still to be commissioned

business.what: Indian electrical equipment maker: power systems (transformers, EHV switchgear), industrial products (motors, railway electronics) and semiconductor units. Earns from product sales and project execution against a large order book.

segments.name: Power Systems
segments.comment: Sales up 31% YoY; PBIT margin rose to 23% on operating leverage.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.comment: Sales up 6%; motors grew double digits; ~INR20 crore railway provision hit PBIT.

segments.name: Semiconductor (CG Semi, Axiro)
segments.comment: Ramp-up investment; ~INR43 crore consolidated drag; Axiro revenue up double digits.

ledger.promise: G2 semiconductor plant to be operational by end-2026 or early 2027, scaling to about 14.5 million chips a day
ledger.quote: G2, which is the main plant... expected to be closed by end of next year or early '27. Once operational, G2 will scale up to the capacity of about 14.5 million chips a day.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 call repeated 'completed by end of calendar year 2026'. Q1 FY27 call said 12–14 month build. The deadline has not arrived and no output data has been reported.

ledger.promise: Transformer capacity to reach 65,000 MVA within about a quarter
ledger.quote: Today, we are already at 40,000, 45,000 MVA, and in a quarter's time we will be 65,000 MVA.
ledger.actual: On the Q4 FY26 call (May 2026), management gave current capacity as 75,000 MVA. That is above the 65,000 MVA promised. The figure comes from the call, not from filings.

ledger.promise: Transformer capacity plan approved by the Board for up to FY28 (about 85,000 MVA) to be finished at least one year early
ledger.quote: as per the plan, that is '27-'28, but the way we are executing, I think we will be much ahead of the target.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 call: 75,000 MVA now, about 1,10,000 MVA by end CY2026. Both are above the ~85,000 MVA FY28 plan. The 1,10,000 MVA figure still needs the new plant to deliver.

ledger.promise: Greenfield transformer plant at Bhopal to be commissioned in July–August 2026 at 25,000–30,000 MVA, rising to 45,000 MVA by end CY2026
ledger.quote: we hope to commission the plant somewhere between July and August. And initially we will be starting with the capacity of around 25,000 to 30,000 MVA
ledger.actual: In July 2026 (Q1 FY27 call) the wording became 'new plant starting up in the next few months'. Whether it was commissioned in Jul–Aug is not shown. The end-CY2026 deadline has not arrived.

ledger.promise: Margin to bounce back in Q3 FY26 as revenue normalises and price hikes flow through
ledger.quote: this basically means that the margin should bounce back into the third quarter once the revenues normalize and full benefit of the price hikes takes place.
ledger.actual: EBITDA margin fell from 12.9% in Q2 FY26 to 12.5% in Q3 FY26. It recovered to 13.5% only in Q4 FY26, a quarter late.

ledger.promise: Railway shipments deferred from Q2 FY26 to come through in Q3 FY26, so revenue only shifts between quarters
ledger.quote: So, we covered some bit of it, but balance will come into this quarter.
ledger.actual: On the Q3 FY26 call management said railways needs 'a few more months' to recover. Q4 FY26 cited competitive railway pricing hurting margin. Q1 FY27 said G.G. Tronics had still not started.

ledger.promise: Final KAVACH approvals to be cleared and shipments started by end-December 2025
ledger.quote: Hopefully, by end of December, we should be in a position to get all this cleared out and start the shipments.
ledger.actual: The date moved three times: to Q4 FY26 (Q3 call), then 'another month, month and a half' (May 2026), then 'next few weeks' (July 2026). Operations had not started by July 2026.

ledger.promise: Axiro subsidiary revenue of about $50 million (about Rs 450 crore) in FY26
ledger.quote: for Axiro, which is our subsidiary, I think they should do approximately $50 million. That is approximately about INR 450 crores, which is very much on track
ledger.actual: No segment figure is provided. The Q3 FY26 call mentioned revenue deferred at Axiro because of holiday timing. No later call reports the FY26 total.

ledger.promise: Rs 748 crore (net of taxes) greenfield switchgear expansion
ledger.quote: the Board of Directors today approved another greenfield expansion for Switchgear business for an investment of INR 748 crores, net of taxes.
ledger.actual: Repeated on the Q4 FY26 call with no completion date. Group capital WIP rose from 386 (FY25) to 725 (FY26) and 846 (FY27). Spending on this project alone is not disclosed.

ledger.promise: Switchgear brownfield ready in a couple of months, adding close to Rs 400 crore revenue
ledger.quote: in the next couple of months, we'll be ready with our brownfield, which is close to our existing facility. That will come up, and I think that itself should give us close to INR 400 crores incremental revenue or sales.
ledger.actual: No later call confirms the brownfield is ready. No switchgear segment revenue is provided.

ledger.promise: Make in India 400 kV GIS to be launched and sold commercially in FY27
ledger.quote: we should be probably coming out with a complete Make in India solution for our 400 kV GIS in the next fiscal year.
ledger.actual: The Q4 FY26 call repeated commercialisation in FY27, with phase-two testing in Q2–Q3 FY27. FY27 has not ended and no update is available.

ledger.promise: CG Semi to break even on about $55–56 million of investment without further funding
ledger.quote: How much? $55 million, $56 million, I think should do that. And I'm very sure with that, we should be able to breakeven, so we don't have to really fund that.
ledger.actual: No breakeven date was given and no segment profit and loss is provided. The Q1 FY27 call said semiconductor losses were rising during ramp-up, mainly from employee costs.

current_guidance.target: About 45,000 MVA more from the new plant
current_guidance.quote: with the new plant starting up in the next few months, I think we will add about 45,000 MVA more into that.

current_guidance.metric: G.G. Tronics Kavach operations and production start
current_guidance.target: Start Kavach operations; consolidated industrial numbers to bounce back
current_guidance.horizon: Next few weeks / within Q2 FY27
current_guidance.quote: definitely in this quarter, they should commence their production. In a quarter or so, it will be bouncing back on that.
hopefully should happen in, I would say, 4 to 6 weeks from now approximately.

current_guidance.target: Build in 12–14 months, against a typical 24–36 months
current_guidance.quote: this kind of plant typically takes about 24 to 36 months. We are doing -- I think we should do hopefully in 12 to 14 months.

current_guidance.metric: Phased capacity ramp (transcript units garbled: GVA/MVA)
current_guidance.target: At least 10,000 in the first quarter, 30,000 in the second, peak 45 in the third
current_guidance.quote: The first phase in the first quarter will be at least 10,000 GVA, going to 30,000 MVA in second quarter and third quarter will be peak at 45 GVA.

current_guidance.target: At least one year ahead of the original FY27–28 plan
current_guidance.quote: our original plan was 2027 financial -- '27, '28 financial year, but I think we should do it at least 1 year before. So just stay tuned with that.

current_guidance.target: Complete IE3, IE4 and IE5 range
current_guidance.quote: the first range across IE3, IE4 and IE5, all this full range will be complete in the next 12 months.

credibility.label: mixed
credibility.summary: On transformer capacity, management did better than promised: it targeted 65,000 MVA and cited 75,000 MVA a quarter later. On short-term calls it did worse: the Q3 FY26 margin rebound did not happen (12.5% vs 12.9%), the deferred railway revenue did not arrive in Q3, and the Kavach start date slipped three times between December 2025 and July 2026. Many semiconductor and subsidiary targets (Axiro revenue, CG Semi breakeven, switchgear brownfield revenue) cannot be checked against these materials, and the larger commissioning dates (G2, Bhopal plant, 400 kV GIS) are still pending.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Q2 FY26 weakness was temporary, and margin would bounce back in Q3 as revenue normalised and price hikes came through.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q3 FY26 revenue rose to 3,175 from 2,923, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 12.9%. Margin recovered to 13.5% only in Q4 FY26.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Most commodity inflation was passed on to customers through steep price increases.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: FY26 EBITDA margin was 13.2% (1,641/12,418) against 13.3% in FY25 (1,319/9,909), roughly flat on revenue up 25.3%. Q2 FY27 margin was 14.2%, the highest of the nine quarters shown.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: The Q1 FY27 shortfall in the industrial business was mainly because G.G. Tronics had not started Kavach, and it would bounce back within a quarter or so.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4.7% from Q4 FY26 (3,281 vs 3,442), and margin was 12.1%, the lowest in the series. Q2 FY27 rebounded to revenue of 3,802 and margin of 14.2%, but whether Kavach drove this cannot be seen.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Growth is presented as orderly, with orders spread evenly across markets and price increases passed through.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Cash from operations fell from 1,028 (FY24) to 916 (FY25) and 702 (FY26), while PAT was 1,199 in FY26, so cash covered only 59% of profit. Debtor days rose from 74 to 86, and the cash conversion cycle from 35 to 48 days.

bull.point: Transformer capacity has been added faster than promised, and the plan now goes well beyond the original FY28 target.
bull.evidence: In Q3 FY26 the target was 65,000 MVA 'in a quarter's time'. On the Q4 FY26 call management cited 75,000 MVA and guided to about 1,10,000 MVA by end CY2026, against an earlier plan of about 85,000 MVA by FY28.
bull.source: Q3 FY26 call p13; Q4 FY26 call p10

bull.point: Reported growth is strong and margin reached a series high in the latest quarter.
bull.evidence: FY26 revenue was 12,418, up 25.3%, and PAT 1,199, up 23.2%. Q2 FY27 revenue was 3,802 (+30.1% YoY), EBITDA 540 (+43.2%), PAT 409 (+44.0%), and EBITDA margin 14.2%.

bull.point: Expansion is being funded without much debt.
bull.evidence: Borrowings were only 118 in FY26 and 169 in FY27, even though the FY26 investing outflow was 3,605 and capital WIP rose to 846.

bear.point: Railway and Kavach timelines keep slipping.
bear.evidence: Approvals and shipments were promised by Dec 2025, then 'this quarter' (Q4 FY26), then 'another month, month and a half' (May 2026), then 'next few weeks' (July 2026). Deferred railway revenue promised for Q3 FY26 became 'a few more months'.
bear.source: Q2 FY26 call p8, p11; Q3 FY26 call p10, p12; Q4 FY26 call p8; Q1 FY27 call p5

bear.point: Working capital is getting worse and cash is falling behind profit.
bear.evidence: Debtor days went from 74 to 86, inventory days from 60 to 67, and the cash conversion cycle from 35 to 48 days (FY25 to FY26). Cash from operations was 702 against PAT of 1,199 in FY26, compared with 916 against 973 in FY25.

bear.point: Semiconductor losses are rising, and the breakeven claim cannot be checked, while core margins have swung.
bear.evidence: In Q1 FY27 management said semiconductor losses were rising, mainly from employee cost. Q4 FY26 standalone PBIT margin was 9.9% vs 12.1%, blamed on mix, railway pricing and tariffs. Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin was 12.1%.
bear.source: Q1 FY27 call p7; Q4 FY26 call p3; reported numbers
